sections.title: Explanation
sections.content: Hungarian often marks the possessor relationship directly on the possessed noun — either as a suffix attached to it, or as a stand-alone possessive pronoun built the same way.

Notice the family resemblance: tiéd is really ti(e) plus the same -d you'd add to a noun for 'your'. Hungarian's 'yours', 'his/hers' and 'ours' pronouns are built on the same person-endings as possessive suffixes — learn the suffixes well and this whole set becomes much easier to remember.
